access_note: Science Data Bank names four public archives totalling about 16.3 GB: aligned visible and SAR imagery with VOC and YOLO annotations. These packages were not downloaded. Training data are airport-detection images, not an airport asset register or operational traffic data.
description: The Aerospace Information Research Institute publishes paired visible-light and synthetic-aperture-radar images for airport detection across China. Google Earth visible images and Gaofen-3 SAR scenes were aligned, and the accompanying labels identify airport targets. The China Scientific Data article reports 1,915 paired samples from 34 provincial-level areas over 2018 to 2020. Science Data Bank lists four archives: visible imagery, SAR imagery, rotated bounding-box VOC annotations and horizontal-box YOLO annotations. Its DataCite rights field states CC BY 4.0. A transport modeller could use the images to train or test airport-location extraction before building an aviation asset or hazard-exposure layer. This is an image-detection benchmark, not an inventory of airport capacity, runways in service or flight flows. The paper reports source-image resolution varying from 8 to 69 metres; imagery and labels may not resolve small support assets. The large archive and annotation coordinates were not downloaded or audited. The catalogued OurAirports record provides airport locations and identifiers, which may serve as a separate reference when checking detected sites. Simulation use therefore requires an additional step from detection output to a checked facility network.
